newsitem.title: USA: NYCE cotton called to open 0.10 cent higher.
newsitem.headline: NYCE cotton called to open 0.10 cent higher.

text.p: NYCE cotton futures were called to open 0.10 cent higher Monday based on market orders at 1019 EST, floor sources said.

National Cotton Council pegged planted acres in 1997/98 at 13.6 million, a seven percent decline from last year. Lost acreage was blamed on favorable prices for competing crops, and provisions in the new Farm Bill giving growers flexibility to plant different crops.
Activity could remain rangebound ahead of USDA's crop report to be released Wednesday.
Friday, the March contract closed 0.13 cent higher at 74.58 cents a lb after trading from 74.90 to 74.30 cents. The back months settled 0.40 to 0.14 firmer.
